land.text: Thalner and Karanda, the Tughlaq fiefs of Malik Raja Faruqi (1370)
Khandesh, annexed by Akbar in January 1601

successors.note: The page does not name the Mughal province.

capitals.name: Thalner
capitals.note: Malik Raja 'established in Thalner on the Tapti River'; Nasir Khan began from Laling (1399).

capitals.name: Asirgarh
capitals.note: Nasir Khan 'captured the fort of Asirgarh' in 1400 and it 'served as his capital at first'; the shift to Burhanpur is undated, so 1437 is a bridging year.

capitals.name: Burhanpur
capitals.note: 'He founded the new capital Burhanpur in 1399.'

rulers.name: Ghazni Khan and Alam Khan
rulers.note: The infobox table is garbled: they are listed under 1508 with no range.

rulers.name: Miran Muhammad Shah I
rulers.note: Died 4 May 1535 and was buried in Burhanpur.

rulers.name: Raja Ali Khan
rulers.note: Died 5 February 1597 in a battle between the Mughals and Ahmadnagar.

rulers.name: Bahadur Shah
rulers.note: Surrendered 10 December 1600; died in Agra in 1624.

correction.text: Khandesh round Thalner and Karanda, the fiefs granted to Malik Raja in 1370

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Khandesh row). 'After receiving the grant of the fiefdoms of Thalner and Karanda' from Firuz Shah Tughluq; 'He began ruling independently by 1382.' The page gives no area or boundary; the gazetteer's Khandesh region (the Tapti valley in Maharashtra) is my reading.

correction.text: Khandesh with Burhanpur and the fort of Asirgarh, captured by Nasir Khan in 1400

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'captured the fort of Asirgarh and killed its Hindu ruler' in 1400; 'He founded the new capital Burhanpur in 1399.' The infobox area is blank on the page. Berar, held in 1435, is not drawn (see ledger).

region.text: Thalner and Karanda on the Tapti

ledger.note: 1382: Malik Raja Faruqi rules Khandesh independently from Thalner. 'from its inception in 1382 till its annexation by the Mughal emperor Akbar in 1601'; 'After receiving the grant of the fiefdoms of Thalner and Karanda' from Firuz Shah Tughluq in 1370; 'He began ruling independently by 1382'. Malik Ahmad (Malik Raja) died in 1399.

1399: Nasir Khan founds Burhanpur. 'He founded the new capital Burhanpur in 1399'; 'He commenced his rule from Laling, as Thalner was under the control of his younger brother Malik Iftikar Hasan'. The page puts the capital at Asirgarh at first and at Burhanpur later, without a year.

region.text: the fort of Asirgarh and Burhanpur

ledger.note: 1400: Nasir Khan takes Asirgarh. Nasir Khan 'captured the fort of Asirgarh and killed its Hindu ruler' in 1400, and it served as his capital at first.
1435: Nasir Khan takes Berar. 'In 1435, Nasir Khan supported by the Raja of Gondwana and some discontented Bahmani officials attacked and captured Berar.' The page does not say how long it was held.
1437: Berar is no longer Khandesh's. The page is silent on the loss; 1437, the year of Nasir Khan's death and of Gujarat's suzerainty, is a bridging year.

1599: Akbar occupies Burhanpur. 'Akbar marched towards Burhanpur in 1599 and occupied the city' (Khandesh page: 'On April 8, 1599, Akbar reached Burhanpur'); Bahadur Shah had 'declared his independence and refused to pay homage'.

1601: Asirgarh falls. Akbar 'besieged Asirgarh fort and captured it on 17 January 1601 by tricking Bahadur Shah'; Bahadur Shah had surrendered on 10 December 1600 but the fort was still held by his general Yakut Khan (Khandesh page).

1601: Khandesh passes to Akbar. 'Asirgarh fell to the Mughals only on January 17, 1601' (marked citation needed on the Khandesh page); Bahadur Shah 'was taken prisoner and he died later in Agra in 1624'.

wars.name: Khandesh-Gujarat wars
wars.outcome: In 1417 Gujarat besieged Thalner and Nasir Khan swore fealty; Miran Adil Khan accepted Gujarat's suzerainty in 1437; in 1498 a Gujarat army entered Khandesh and Adil Khan II agreed to pay the arrears.

wars.name: Khandesh-Bahmani war over Berar
wars.outcome: Nasir Khan, with the Raja of Gondwana, captured Berar in 1435; the page gives no result.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Khandesh
wars.outcome: Akbar reached Burhanpur on 8 April 1599, Bahadur Shah surrendered on 10 December 1600 and Asirgarh fell on 17 January 1601.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on the pages opened; the Khandesh frontiers are approximate.

sources.title: Khandesh Sultanate

sources.title: Asirgarh Fort

notes:
No Cliopatria row. Two pages (Khandesh Sultanate; Asirgarh Fort, which is thin) were opened for this dossier; the Malik Raja Faruqi and Nasir Khan Faruqi pages do not exist under those titles. The page gives no area, boundary or capital dates, so both keyframes are readings.
Disagreements: 1382 (inception) against the 1370 fief grant and Malik Raja's reign '1382-1399'; Burhanpur 'founded 1399' but the capital at Asirgarh 'at first'; the Khandesh page says 'Akbar annexed Gujarat in 1572 CE' (Gujarat's dossier has 1573); the 17 January 1601 fall is marked citation needed.
Not settled: how long Berar was held after 1435 (loss at confidence 1); when the capital moved to Burhanpur; the 1417 siege of Thalner and Khandesh's fealty (Gujarat holds the vassal events from 1437); the 1561 refuge of Baz Bahadur; the 1574 Ahmadnagar annexation of Berar; the Mughal province name (Khandesh Subah, not on the pages).
Counterparts: gujarat-sultanate (vassal_start 1437 is in its ledger, with an end bridged to 1573), malwa-sultanate, bahmani-sultanate (sa-04-c), berar-sultanate (sa-04-d), mughal-empire (sa-05-a).
